propositions: The test intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300-second per-test timeout guard

The test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent: measured 91.6s idle but 504.8s under saturating CPU pressure (1.7x past 300s guard), because it processes ~1768 serial pandoc spawns across 884 renderable units in a single monolithic loop
pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) from its timer thread, killing the worker outright with no traceback rather than failing the test
The fix chunks the equivalence test into fixed-size batches parametrized by index, ensuring per-test cost is bounded by construction and independent of corpus size
A new coverage guard test verifies all chunks reassemble to the original unit list while preserving byte-identity validation and real pandoc comparisons
The fix reduces worst-case cost from 504.8s to 38.05s under identical saturation, providing 7.9x headroom within the 300s budget
